result.topic_en: Gauss notes Euler's result that the integral from 0 to 1 of sqrt(log(1/x)) dx equals half the square root of pi, and by a substitution and integration by parts reduces it to the Gaussian integral of e^{-t^2} from 0 to infinity.
result.transcription:
Math 28
Euler gibt Comment. nov. Ac. Petr. 16 p. 101
den Satz  (16) [-48c/16-]
$\int_0^1 dx\sqrt{\log\frac{1}{x}} = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\pi}$
setzt man $\frac{1}{x} = e^{-tt}$
so verwandelt sich
$dx.\sqrt{\log\frac{1}{x}}$ in $-2tt\,e^{-tt}dt$
und es ist also jener Satz gleichb.[?] mit
$\int_0^\infty tte^{-tt}dt = \frac{1}{4}\sqrt{\pi}$
Es ist aber
$2tte^{-tt}dt = -d\{te^{-tt}\} + e^{-tt}dt$
Also
$\int_0^\infty e^{-tt}dt = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\pi}.$

methods.what: Euler's integral of the square root of log(1/x) over [0,1]
Substitution relating log(1/x) to t^2 (written 1/x = e^{-tt} on the page)
Equivalent form: integral of t^2 e^{-t^2} from 0 to infinity
